narrative.summary: Knockout (KO) and wild-type (WT) samples, 3 of each, were compared while accounting for sex. 37 genes changed significantly: 12 higher and 25 lower in KO. The strongest change is a decrease of Geny9 (log2 fold change -6.62). Sex explains more of the main variation between samples than genotype does, and sample KO_2 clusters with the WT samples. Pathway analysis was not run because the gene IDs could not be matched to gene names. Because one KO sample looks like a WT sample, these results should be checked before they are relied on.
key_findings: 37 genes pass the significance rule: 12 higher and 25 lower in KO.
Geny9 has the largest decrease in KO (log2 fold change -6.62, adjusted p-value 1.2e-30).
PC1 (38.0% of the variance) is explained more by sex (0.52) than by genotype (0.41).
KO_2 clusters with the WT samples.
narrative.sample_structure: PC1 explains 38.0% and PC2 22.5% of the variance; sex accounts for more of PC1 than genotype. KO_2 clusters with the WT samples rather than with the other KO samples.
narrative.gene_highlights: Geny9 (example gene y9) is much lower in KO (log2 fold change -6.62). Genx3 (example gene x3) is the top gene higher in KO (log2 fold change 2.08).
narrative.pathway_highlights: Pathway analysis was not run: no tested genes have gene symbols, so gene sets cannot be matched.
caveats: KO_2 clusters with the WT samples, which can mean a mislabelled sample or an incomplete knockout.
With 3 samples per group, smaller changes may be missed.
next_steps: Check the genotype of KO_2 (for example, the expression of the knocked-out gene in the gene table).
If KO_2 was mislabelled or failed, rerun the analysis leaving it out (Advanced settings, Leave samples out).
